result:
February 2026 revenue was lower because February had fewer high-sales days, not because sales got weaker. Revenue per day, per unit and in every channel held steady.

## The numbers
| | Jan 2026 | Feb 2026 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (INR) | ₹529.8M | ₹460.7M | **−₹69.1M (−13.0%)** |
| Units sold | 904,945 | 787,119 | −13.0% |
| Revenue per unit | ~₹585.5 | ~₹585.4 | flat |

## What caused it
**1. It wasn't one channel.** Every channel fell by the same amount, about 13%:

| Channel | Jan | Feb | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLATFORM | 154.4M | 134.2M | −13.0% |
| D2C | 119.3M | 103.8M | −13.0% |
| QCOMM | 99.9M | 86.9M | −13.1% |
| OFFLINE | 61.9M | 53.8M | −13.1% |
| INTERNATIONAL | 59.0M | 51.3M | −13.1% |
| CAFE | 35.3M | 30.8M | −13.0% |

Discount rates didn't move either (OFFLINE ~9.8%, PLATFORM ~6.1%), so pricing and promotions aren't the cause.

**2. Daily revenue comes in two levels.**
- **Normal days:** about ₹11.5M.
- **High days:** about ₹23M. These are every Saturday and Sunday, plus a high-sales stretch near month-end (Jan 23–Feb 1 and Feb 24–28).

**3. February had 3 fewer high days.**

| | High days (~₹23M) | Normal days (~₹11.5M) | Total days |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | 15 (9 weekend + 6 month-end weekdays) | 16 | 31 |
| Feb | 12 (8 weekend + 4 month-end weekdays) | 16 | 28 |

Both months had exactly 16 normal days. February's 3 missing days were all high days: one fewer weekend day and two fewer weekdays in the month-end stretch. 3 × ~₹23M ≈ ₹69M, which matches the whole drop.

**Bottom line:** most of the gap is February having 3 fewer days. The rest comes from which days those were (the weekend and month-end days that sell double). Average revenue per day fell from ₹17.1M to ₹16.5M only because of that day mix. On a like-for-like day, sales were the same.

**Worth flagging:** the data is unusually uniform. Every day's total sits within about 1% of one of two levels, and all six channels moved by exactly 13%. If this is real production data, check whether it's synthetic or seeded before acting on it.

I used the `sales.revenue_inr` measure from the `sales` semantic-layer source, which combines all six channels and excludes deleted rows. I also saved this finding to ktx memory, including the note that month-over-month comparisons should be adjusted for day mix.
